key_insight: Flexible, modular robots can move and manipulate objects individually, then physically connect into task-adaptive forms. This lets them cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Robots with fixed body shapes can struggle when different tasks demand different physical capabilities. This work addresses the need for robotic systems that adapt both their configuration and their cooperation to the task.
method: Use flexible tensegrity continuum robot modules that combine locomotion and manipulation in a single unit.
Physically connect modules to create cooperative, task-adaptive configurations.
Apply these configurations to object transport, gap crossing and challenging-terrain navigation.
impact: For AI and robotics practitioners, the work highlights body configuration as another dimension of adaptive behavior, alongside control. It motivates planning and coordination methods that consider how robots should connect and reshape for a task.
visual_elements: Single-module diagram highlighting its flexible structure, movement and object-handling capabilities.
Sequence showing individual modules connecting into different cooperative configurations.
Three-panel task illustration: carrying an object, crossing a gap and navigating uneven terrain.
Task-to-configuration map linking each challenge to a suitable robot arrangement.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
